transcription.text: Hi, welcome to the EEVblog. I'm your host, Dave Jones, and this is episode number 22.
I was going to try and keep this blog on topic, you know, talking about stuff of interest to
electronics engineers, but I thought, you know, we've done over 20 of these blogs so far, so I
thought I'd do a bit of a Q&A, a bit of, you know, questions and answers, because I get a lot of
questions and a lot of them are the same, and I thought I'd just talk about my experiences with
video blogging, because it's a first for me and, you know, some other people out there might want
to know, you know, things I've found along the way as well. So, let's talk about blogs and blogging.
Probably the most common thing I get asked is, do I use a script, you know, is all this blog
stuff scripted? Do I think about it before I do it? Do I put any research into it? And the
answer's in the title of the video blog, my tagline, an off-the-cuff video blog about electronics
engineering. So, the answer is no, it's not scripted. I don't have a script, virtually never,
and I really don't think about stuff before I sit in front of the camera and yap on.
Basically, what I do is, usually in the morning before I head out to work or something, I will
sit down for about 15 minutes and I'll sit in front of the camera and go, right, what am I
going to talk about? Well, sometimes I'll have an idea what I'm going to talk about, but I basically
just sit in front of the camera and rabbit on. I haven't really thought about, you know,
key points or things like that. I just sit here and so, hence why I'm rabbiting on now, because,
you know, I haven't thought about this. So, there you go. It's an off-the-cuff video blog.
And the reason I did that is because, you know, I thought it would be more personal. I thought it
would be a bit more entertaining than, you know, me sitting here reading a script and sounding like
I have scripted my lines and trying to talk in a nice, fluid way so everyone understands me. But
no! I talk in my usual fast-paced, whiny Aussie accent and, you know, this is me. So, you know,
I like to think that the blog is basically, you know, me just, you know, chatting around the
water cooler with you guys every week or once or twice a week and, you know, and that's what it
basically is. Rabbiting on! People also ask, you know, how much stuff do I film for each blog? And,
well, the answer's about probably 15 minutes, 15, you know, 20, like a really long and complex one.
I might, it might go up to 25, but generally average is just over, you know, 15, 18 minutes
worth of footage, something like that. And I've got to edit that down into 10 minutes. And that's
really hard because that's a YouTube, I upload my videos onto YouTube and they only allow you
10 minutes. So that's where the 10-minute limitation comes from. And most people have
commented that 10 minutes is probably, you know, it's borderline too long anyway. So, you know,
I want some feedback on that because this is new to me. I just got the idea that I'd, you know,
go ahead and, you know, jump right in and do this as I explained in my first blog. And
the biggest really annoying thing about video blogging I found is that, you know, I don't get
a second chance to do anything. I sit here in front of the camera, I rabbit on for, you know,
15, you know, 15, 20 minutes and, you know, I get off to work, I come home and I'll, you know,
upload the video and I go, you know, and I'll watch it and I'll go, oh, that's crap, I didn't
mean to say that or I should have explained it better, you know, in some way. Oh, that's wrong
what I've done there and it's not really right, that's not, wasn't my intention. But I can't
really go back and film it because I don't have the time. So really, it's, you know, a lot of
times I've had to just go ahead with the blog so I get something out there even though I know it
might be a bit, you know, a bit wrong or not really what I intended or I've had to cut parts
out of it and, you know, but I've really had to, you know, swallow my pride of, you know,
doing things, you know, right and with video blogging and that still gets at me, you know,
because I've got to release these blogs, I think. I'd rather just have them going out there
otherwise I'd never, if I refined it and tweaked it and re-filmed things to explain things
perfectly, I'd never get the blogs out there. So, you know, it's an off-the-cuff blog and that's
the chance I take. So yes, there's a ton of stuff which doesn't actually make it into the final
blog and it's really annoying to me, you know, there's lots of stuff I go, oh no, I've got to
leave that out because I've got to squeeze an extra two seconds in here to fit the 10-minute
limit and there's, you know, some really meaty valuable stuff that doesn't make it and it bugs
me. But, you know, such is life of a video blogger. Now, Paul Rakow of the Analog Blog who got all
the RF guys onto my oscilloscope phenomenon thing, he, which they haven't replied to, by the way,
they're all suddenly a bit silent after my second set of blogs, you know, proved it wasn't the
ground loop, so, you know, come on fellas. Now, he made the point that I make, I take too long in
my video blogs to make my point and, you know, he's probably right. But, you know, it's, video
is all about, you know, storytelling, you know, it's, you know, telling the yarn. I'm Australian,
I like to tell a good yarn and, you know, it's all about storytelling and being personal so that,
you know, he says, you know, he made the point that text blogs and diagrams and things pre-prepared
and pre-done are more accurate. Yeah, they're more accurate but they're pretty boring and, you know,
I didn't want to create just another text blog. There's, you know, there's countless ones out
there but there's no video blogs. So, I thought I'd do a video blog and at least some people seem
to like it anyway. I got a rather interesting comment once, in fact, I've had it more than
once in various forms but the comment was basically, how do we know you're right? How
can we take your word for it on, you know, all these things and all these topics? And, well,
you know, it's a really good question and the answer is you shouldn't. You should never take
anyone's word for it. Don't take anything I say on these blogs as gospel. You know, I've been in
the industry for 20 years so, you know, I like to think I do know what I'm talking about mostly.
But, you know, don't take my word for it. All my blogs and all the things I talk about on here
are designed to be food for thought. You're supposed to use your own engineering judgment
and, you know, go out and verify things. If you're, you know, if you're really interested
in something, don't complain that I didn't explain it right or, you know, I might have
got it a bit wrong or something like that. Go out and investigate for yourself. That's what it's all
about. Food for thought. There's another question I get asked fairly regularly. Is this my own home
lab? And, yes, it is. This is out in my garage here. It's only tiny. It's only, you know, a couple of
meters by a couple of meters but it serves the purpose and, no, this is not my place of work.
This is just my home hobby lab. Another question is, you know, do I get paid for doing this? Well,
the answer is no. It's, you know, it's done because I think it's fun and that's it. Do I get paid by
the manufacturers? No. A lot of people said that I was paid by Fluke because I keep promoting their
gear and stuff like that. No. God no. They won't even send me their stuff. And do I get, do the
manufacturers send me equipment? No, they don't. They're too scared to, I think. Either that or
they don't know I exist and which is most likely the case. I get a lot of feedback about what people
want to see in the blog and please keep sending me this stuff. You know, keep sending me ideas
because, you know, I'm not really short of ideas. I've got sort of a little notepad book where I
might jot down a few ideas for some future blogs but generally I sort of, you know, make them up,
you know. I really haven't gotten through that list much yet so it's because I always think
about something else to do. So please keep sending them through. I read all your emails and I try and
respond where possible and I'm really after some good ideas. So please send me your feedback. Each
video blog has a little comment section. You can add comments to each blog and I don't censor them
so, you know, if you want to say something's crap, say it. I'll post it, you know. I'm not scared of,
you know, people giving me negative feedback. I think it's great. It promotes discussion and,
you know, it's really fun. An interesting little fact is that about 15% of my viewers via
YouTube anyway are female and that's really cool. That's actually quite surprising too because,
you know, it's a highly male-dominated industry and I might go into some stats in some later
blogs. I might actually show you some stats I get but, yeah, that's really cool. Keep it up,
girls. I hope you enjoy it.
